title: South Dakota Governor Election, 2026
description: The 2026 South Dakota gubernatorial election is scheduled for November 3, 2026, to elect the governor for a four-year term. Incumbent Republican Governor Larry Rhoden, who ascended from lieutenant governor in January 2025 after Kristi Noem resigned to become U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security, is seeking his first full term. The Republican primary on June 2 ended without a candidate reaching the required 35% threshold, triggering a July 28 runoff between Rhoden and Aberdeen businessman Toby Doeden. Former state legislator Dan Ahlers is the Democratic nominee. South Dakota has not elected a Democratic governor since 1974 and currently has a Republican trifecta in state government, making this a heavily Republican-leaning race.
polling_note: No general-election matchup polls between the Democratic nominee and either Republican candidate were found. Available polls from 2025-2026 focused on the multi-candidate Republican primary, which has since concluded with Rhoden and Doeden advancing to a July 28 runoff.

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
candidates.summary: Larry Rhoden is the incumbent Governor of South Dakota, having assumed office on January 25, 2025, after Kristi Noem resigned to join the Trump administration. A lifelong rancher and welder from Union Center, Rhoden previously served as lieutenant governor from 2019 to 2025 and in both chambers of the South Dakota Legislature for a combined 14 years. He is campaigning on his record of signing legislation to reduce homeowner property taxes, ban eminent domain for carbon pipelines, and fund a new state prison.

candidates.name: Toby Doeden
candidates.summary: Toby Doeden is an Aberdeen businessman and political newcomer who advanced to the July 28 Republican primary runoff by finishing first in the June 2 primary with 31% of the vote. He owns multiple businesses including car dealerships, rental properties, and retail establishments. Doeden is running as a political outsider and strong supporter of President Donald Trump, vowing to phase out property taxes, reduce state spending, and bring a business-oriented approach to state government. He has invested at least $4 million of his own money into his campaign.

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
candidates.summary: Dan Ahlers is the Democratic nominee for Governor of South Dakota, having run uncontested in the June 2 Democratic primary. A former state senator and state representative from Dell Rapids, Ahlers also served as executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party and was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2020. He is a small business owner who emphasizes his experience working across party lines in the legislature and his focus on common-sense solutions to issues like education funding, rising costs, and rural community vitality.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling is available, so this forecast relies on the race description and candidate context rather than numeric head-to-head data. South Dakota is described as a heavily Republican-leaning state with a current Republican trifecta, and it has not elected a Democratic governor since 1974. The GOP is favored to retain the office regardless of whether incumbent Larry Rhoden or runoff challenger Toby Doeden is the eventual nominee, and Rhoden is provisionally listed as the predicted winner because he is the incumbent and remains in the runoff. Confidence is reduced to medium because the Republican nominee is not yet finalized and there are no general-election polls.
